document_info.title: Global Reforestation Species Database
document_info.description: A comprehensive list of tree and vegetation species suitable for reforestation, detailed by climatic suitability, stress tolerance, and environmental impact.

stress_tolerance.drought: High - Can survive in regions with rainfall as low as 400mm.
stress_tolerance.flood: Low - Does not tolerate waterlogging well.
stress_tolerance.high_aqi: High - Excellent at trapping dust and absorbing pollutants.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Thrives in rocky, shallow, and poor soils.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Moderate to High. Rapid biomass accumulation in early years.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: improves soil fertility by reducing acidity and mining nutrients from deep soil layers. Leaves act as natural mulch.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Deep taproot system helps stabilize the water table.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Releases high amounts of oxygen and acts as a natural air purifier against SO2 and NO2.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: As a sapling, it acts as a soil binder. As a mature tree, it provides a dense canopy that significantly lowers ambient ground temperature and supports insect biodiversity.

stress_tolerance.drought: Moderate - Deep rooting allows survival in dry spells once established.
stress_tolerance.frost: High - Very hardy against cold winters.
stress_tolerance.high_aqi: Moderate - Can tolerate urban environments but sensitive to acute smog.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: Moderate - Prefers deep, fertile soil but adapts to heavy clay.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Very High. Long-lived species that stores carbon for centuries.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Leaf litter creates rich humus, significantly improving topsoil quality over decades.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: High transpiration rates contribute to cloud formation; roots prevent erosion.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Filters particulate matter efficiently due to large leaf surface area.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Saplings require protection from herbivores. Mature trees become 'keystone species,' supporting more wildlife (birds, insects, fungi) than almost any other tree type.

stress_tolerance.drought: N/A - Adapted to saline water, but sensitive to hypersalinity if freshwater flow stops.
stress_tolerance.flood: Extreme - Lives permanently in waterlogged, tidal zones.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Adapted to anaerobic, nutrient-poor coastal soils.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Extreme (Blue Carbon). Sequesters carbon in sediment 10x faster than terrestrial forests.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Builds land by trapping sediment in prop roots; prevents coastal erosion.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Filters runoff water, removing nitrates and phosphates before they reach the ocean.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Local cooling effect on coastal zones.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Saplings stabilize immediate mudflats. Mature forests act as critical barriers against storm surges and tsunamis, protecting inland areas.

stress_tolerance.drought: Extreme - Stores thousands of liters of water in its trunk.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Thrives in poor, rocky soils.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Moderate per tree, but critical in sparse landscapes.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Prevents desertification; fallen leaves enrich poor savanna soils.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Acts as a living reservoir, maintaining local humidity.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Minor direct filtration, but stabilizes dust.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Saplings are slow-growing. Mature trees create distinct micro-ecosystems, providing shade and shelter for hundreds of species in harsh heat.

stress_tolerance.drought: Moderate - Rhizomes can survive dry spells, though growth slows.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Can reclaim degraded land rapidly.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Extreme (Short-term). Absorbs carbon 4x faster than many hardwood trees.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Extensive root mat prevents landslides and severe erosion.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Raises water table by reducing runoff speed.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Releases 35% more oxygen than equivalent stands of trees.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Reaches full height in months/years rather than decades. Rapidly creates canopy cover, protecting soil from UV radiation and heavy rain impact.

stress_tolerance.high_aqi: Extreme - Specifically adapted to shed bark, removing absorbed pollutants.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Tolerates compacted, poor urban soils.

environmental_effects.soil_profile: Can break up compacted soil over time.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Manages storm water runoff in paved areas.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Exceptional at trapping particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10) on hairy leaves and bark.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Saplings are robust. Mature trees provide massive shade canopies (reducing urban heat island effect) and are resilient to physical damage.

stress_tolerance.drought: Moderate - Surprisingly drought tolerant once established.
stress_tolerance.flood: Extreme - Can live permanently in standing water.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: High - Long lifespan leads to significant biomass storage.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Knees (pneumatophores) trap sediment and stabilize river banks.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Filters pollutants from river water; slows floodwaters.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: As it matures, it develops a buttressed base that acts as a physical barrier against water flow erosion, critical for maintaining wetland integrity.

stress_tolerance.drought: High - Adapted to sandy, well-drained soils.
stress_tolerance.high_aqi: Moderate - Can suffer in high sulfur dioxide areas.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: High - Needs very little nitrogen to thrive.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: High - Dense wood stores significant carbon in cold climates.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Needle drop acidifies soil (can be negative for some flora, good for fungi).
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Canopy intercepts heavy snowfall, regulating meltwater release.
environmental_effects.air_quality: Produces terpenes which interact with atmospheric chemistry; filters dust year-round.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Saplings are pioneer species in open ground. Mature stands create a unique microclimate that shelters understory species from wind and extreme cold.

stress_tolerance.drought: High - Roots penetrate up to 3-4 meters.
stress_tolerance.flood: High - Can survive complete submergence for weeks.
stress_tolerance.nutrient_depletion: Extreme - Grows in toxic, saline, or metal-heavy soils.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: Moderate (Soil Carbon). Sequesters carbon deep in the soil profile via roots.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: The gold standard for erosion control; anchors soil on steep slopes.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: Increases groundwater recharge by 20-30% by slowing runoff.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Non-invasive (sterile seeds). Forms a dense hedge that physically blocks sediment runoff and treats wastewater by absorbing nitrates and phosphates.

stress_tolerance.drought: Low - Requires access to water table.

environmental_effects.carbon_sequestration: High rate (fast growth), but shorter lifespan than oaks.
environmental_effects.soil_profile: Rapid leaf turnover builds topsoil quickly.
environmental_effects.water_cycle: High water uptake can help drain swampy areas.
environmental_effects.maturation_impact: Acts as a 'nurse tree' providing quick shade that allows slower-growing, long-term species (like hardwoods) to establish underneath.
